newsitem.title: USA: U.S. EPA to give Intel plant simpler air permit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. EPA to give Intel plant simpler air permit.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency reached an agreement with Intel Corp to simplify its environmental reporting requirements at a new semiconductor plant in return for meeting tighter air pollution standards, EPA said Monday.

Under the agreement, to be signed Tuesday, EPA will give Intel a single air permit for its new Chandler, Arizona plant, instead of requiring the plant to obtain separate pollution permits for each of its manufacturing processes.

The company would also be exempt from having to update its permit everytime it wanted to alter a manufacturing process, and would be allowed to file a single air, land, and water pollution report to Maricopa County, instead of filing different reports to several agencies.
In return for the simpler permit, the company agreed to adopt a five-year plan to use new pollution prevention techniques and increase solid waste recycling.
The agreement is part of the EPA's Project XL, designed to cut regulatory red tape.
